chunks: And let not the virtuous and the vicious be in an equal position before you,
for in that is dissuasion of the people of virtue from virtue, and training of the people of vice upon vice. And bind each of them to what they bound themselves to.

And know that nothing is more conducive to the good impression of a ruler upon his subjects than his good behavior towards them, lightening the burdens upon them, and refraining from forcing them to do what is not incumbent upon them,
so let there be from you in that a matter by which you gather good impression with your subjects,
for good impression cuts off from you long toil,
and indeed the most deserving of your good impression is he upon whom your trial has been good, and indeed the most deserving of your bad impression is he upon whom your trial has been bad.
ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of justice and administration in Imam Ali's letter to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: This passage from the Letter to Malik al-Ashtar underscores the psychological mechanics of justice, warning that equating the good and bad erodes incentive for virtue while encouraging vice. Imam Ali (AS) further elaborates on the reciprocal nature of governance, asserting that a ruler's benevolence and fairness cultivate trust (husn al-zann) among subjects, thereby reducing administrative friction and ensuring that those who prove reliable during trials are the ones most worthy of confidence.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The virtuous and the vicious should not be in equal position before you
because this means dissuasion of the virtuous from virtue and persuasion of the vicious to vice. Keep everyone in the position which is his.

You should know that the most conducive thing for the good impression of the ruler on his subjects is that he should extend good behaviour towards them, lighten their hardships, and avoid putting them to unbearable troubles.
You should therefore, in this way follow a course by which you will leave a good impression with your subjects
, because such good ideas will relieve you of great worries.
Certainly, the most appropriate for good impression of you is he to whom your behaviour has not been good.
